s016.description:
Was 1 rupee equal to 1 dollar in 1947? The rupee vs dollar myth, fact-checked.
Rupee to dollar history: 1947, 1966, 1991 and today's near-record low.

In 1947 the rupee was pegged to the British pound, and a US dollar cost about ₹3.31 — never ₹1. India devalued to ₹7.50 per dollar in 1966, and after the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis the rate passed ₹30 within a year. In May 2026 the rupee hit a record low near ₹97; on 29 Oct 2026 it traded around ₹95. A weaker rupee also makes Indian exports cheaper abroad. Not financial advice.

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange_rate_history_of_the_Indian_rupee
https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/rupee-near-record-low-why-rbis-multiple-defences-are-losing-effectiveness-560381-2026-10-08
https://www.etvbharat.com/en/business/rupee-vs-us-dollar-on-october-29-2026-enn26102901004

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #rupee #dollar
s016.comment: What did your grandparents tell you about 1947? 👇 Fact: in 1947 a dollar cost about ₹3.31 — the rupee was tied to the British pound.

s017.description:
Pig butchering scam explained: how a "wrong number" text turns into a fake crypto investment.
How the crypto romance scam works and the warning signs.

Scammers build trust for weeks, then introduce a crypto app that shows huge fake profits and even lets you withdraw a little. When you try to cash out a bigger amount, a "tax" or fee appears — and the money is gone. The FBI's IC3 2025 report counts about $7.2 billion lost to cryptocurrency investment fraud. On 27 Oct 2026 US prosecutors charged a ring whose workers were paid bonuses tied to the amounts stolen.

Sources:
https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf
https://www.avasc.org/briefings/ftc-fake-deactivation-calls-escalate-as-doj-charges-crypto-romance-ring-2026-10-28

s017.comment: Ever got a "wrong number" text? 👇 FBI IC3: about $7.2 billion was lost to crypto investment fraud in 2025.

s018.description:
Mansa Musa in Cairo, 1324: how one king's gold made gold cheaper for about 12 years.
The Mali emperor's pilgrimage to Mecca and its effect on Cairo's gold price.

On his way to Mecca, Mansa Musa gave gold to Cairo's officials, emirs and treasury, and his party spent freely. The chronicler al-Umari wrote that a mithqal of gold, which had never fetched less than 25 silver dirhams, fell to 22 dirhams or less, and stayed low for about twelve years. Caravan sizes and the "tons of gold" are legend-level estimates.

Sources:
https://www.digitalhistory.uh.edu/active_learning/explorations/1492/mansa_musa_visit.cfm

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #history #gold
